needs_table:
- idea.summary: Your idea in one line
- audience.segments: Who it is for
- roles.list: Roles
- scope.must_not: What it must not do
- devices.profile: Devices
- look.tone_words: Tone and mood
- context.geo: Country and city

needs.label: Your idea in one line
needs.sufficient: One or two sentences that say what the app does and for whom, in the user's own words.

needs.label: Who it is for
needs.sufficient: At least one named segment: who they are, their main goal, and where and how they use the app. Separate the paying customer from the end user when they differ.

needs.label: Roles
needs.sufficient: Each distinct kind of person who signs in: their top goal and what they can approve or change.

needs.label: What it must not do
needs.sufficient: Anything the app must explicitly not do or include.

needs.label: Devices
needs.sufficient: Which devices the users have: phone only, phone and tablet, low-end phones.

needs.label: Tone and mood
needs.sufficient: Two or three words for the mood and personality the app should have.

needs.label: Country and city
needs.sufficient: Country; city or region (or nationwide); the languages spoken there; and whether it starts in one city or several.

kinds.description: A business rule, policy or functional requirement the app must follow or enforce.
A quantity, limit, price, percentage, duration or other figure the app depends on.
A condition that must hold for a feature to count as done.
A screen, page or view and what it shows or lets the person do.
A sequence of steps a person goes through to get something done.
A thing the app keeps track of (a record, a document, an item) and what is known about it.
A law, regulation, consent, privacy or certification requirement.
A quality the app must have (speed, offline use, security, accessibility, reliability, scale).
An outside system, service or interface and how the app uses it.
A limit on how the app is built or run (budget, deadline, platform, must use, must not).
A sample case, number or situation that illustrates how something should work.
A taste, style or wish that is not a hard requirement.
Background about the business, the people, the place or the goal.
A detail that fits none of the kinds above; every agent may need it.
